q-250394.name: Question 1
q-250394.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}+2ax+{a}^{2}=(x+a)^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+18x+81 & = \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 9x+{9}^{2} & = \\ (x+9)^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}+18x+81)+5 & = \\ (x+9)^{2}+5 & .\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: x+9
5

q-250441.name: Question 3
q-250441.worked_solution:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a)^{2}

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-4x+4)-10 & = \\ (x-2)^{2}-10 & .\end{aligned}

q-141532.name: Question 4
q-141532.problem: Rewrite the expression $({x}^{2}-8x+16)-2$ as the difference between a perfect square and a constant.
q-141532.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a)^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8x+16 & = \\ {x}^{2}-8x+{4}^{2} & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 4x+{4}^{2} & = \\ (x-4)^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-8x+16)-2 & = \\ (x-4)^{2}-2 & .\end{aligned}
$$

a
(x−8)2−2
b
(x+8)2−2
c
(x+4)2−2
d
(x−4)2−2
e
(x−16)2−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the following formula: x2−2ax+a2=(x−a)2

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows: x2−8x+16=x2−8x+42=x2−2⋅4x+42=(x−4)2

Therefore, we obtain (x2−8x+16)−2=(x−4)2−2.

q-250450.name: Question 5
q-250450.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{y}^{2}+2\cdot 10y+106
$$

Now, here's the trick. We *add* and *then subtract* ${10}^{2},$ writing the constant term $106$ last:

$$
{{y}^{2}+2\cdot 10y+{10}^{2}}_{⏟}-\,{10}^{2}+106
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(y+10)^{2}-{10}^{2}+106
$$

Finally, evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(y+10)^{2}+6.
$$

$$

q-141622.name: Question 7
q-141622.problem: If the expression ${y}^{2}-10y+30$ is written as $(y+p)^{2}+q,$ then what are the values of $p$ and $q?$
q-141622.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{y}^{2}-2\cdot 5y+30
$$

Now, here's the trick. We *add* and *then subtract* ${5}^{2},$ writing the constant term $30$ last:

$$
{{y}^{2}-2\cdot 5y+{5}^{2}}_{⏟}-\,{5}^{2}+30
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(y-5)^{2}-{5}^{2}+30
$$

Finally, evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(y-5)^{2}+5.
$$

Therefore, $p=-5$ and $q=5.$
